mode: agent
description: 'Initialize this site repository from a source project frontend and import its generated site artifact for the first time.'

# Import a frontend into this site repository

Bind this repository to one frontend of a source project and import that frontend's
generated site artifact.

The frontend to publish is: `${input:frontend:Absolute path to the frontend directory, e.g. C:\projects\absent-from-chronic\_frontend-1}`

If the user supplied a path in the invocation text, use that instead of prompting.

## Rules

- Never modify anything inside the source project. It is read-only for this workflow.
- Never copy source files (`.qmd`, `.R`, `.Rmd`, notebooks), private data, `.env` files,
  or build caches into this repository. `scripts/initialize-site.ps1` enforces this;
  do not work around a refusal, report it.
- Never edit files under the artifact directory by hand. They are generated bytes and
  must match the source exactly.
- Do not commit or push unless the user explicitly asks.

## Procedure

1. **Resolve the frontend.**
   Confirm the supplied path exists. If it names a project root rather than a frontend,
   list the candidate frontend directories (`_frontend-*`, `frontend-*`, `site/`, `docs/`)
   and ask the user which one to publish. Do not guess when more than one candidate exists.

2. **Confirm the frontend has been rendered.**
   The frontend must contain a generated site subdirectory (`_site` by default) with a
   root `index.html`. If it is missing, stop and tell the user to render the frontend in
   the source project first — rendering must not happen in this repository, because the
   private inputs are not here.

3. **Dry run.**

   ```powershell
   ./scripts/initialize-site.ps1 -FrontendPath '<absolute-frontend-path>'
   ```

   Report back: the detected source project and remote URL, the frontend directory, the
   file count, the detected entry point and landing page, and the add/change/delete
   counts from the transfer preview. Surface every warning verbatim.

4. **Confirm the site title.**
   The script derives a title from the source repository name. Show it to the user and
   let them override with `-SiteTitle`. Do not invent a title of your own.

5. **Apply.**

   ```powershell
   ./scripts/initialize-site.ps1 -FrontendPath '<absolute-frontend-path>' -Apply
   ```

   Add `-SiteTitle '<title>'` when the user supplied one. Add `-AllowDelete` only when
   the preview showed deletions and the user approved them explicitly.

6. **Verify the result.**
   - `site.config.json` records the source project, frontend, and landing page.
   - `README.md` and `netlify.toml` are rendered with no `{{TOKEN}}` placeholders left.
   - `git status --short` shows changes only under the artifact directory plus
     `site.config.json`, `README.md`, and `netlify.toml`.
   - Delete `_site/.gitkeep` once the artifact directory holds real content.

7. **Check the site renders.**
   When browser tools are available, serve the artifact directory locally and confirm the
   root entry point, the landing page, navigation, and images resolve. Report anything broken
   rather than patching generated HTML.

8. **Summarize and hand off.**
   State what was imported, what remains to be configured outside the repository
   (static host project settings, or enabling GitHub Pages), and that the user should
   review the diff before committing.

## Follow-up

Routine content refreshes after initialization use `/publish-site`, not this prompt.
